checks.finding: Verified the round-1 fix on its merits. requirements.md:84-95 (AC-030) now enumerates four parts -- (1) push failure does not change consent state, (2) agent reports the failure, (3) same-scope retry proceeds without a new consent prompt and re-enters at the AC-017 pre-upload check point, (4) the failure is explicitly distinguished from AC-019's persistent 'not permitted' outcome (no standing forbiddance) -- each with its own vacuous-satisfaction rationale at :95, mirroring AC-026's model at :58-64 where the equivalent decline/persistent-outcome distinction is its own numbered element (row 3) matched by TEST-043. acceptance-tests.md:61 (matrix row) and :246-248 (detail block for TEST-051) now enumerate the identical four parts in the identical order, and the detail block states explicitly 'the assertion set and the criterion's own numbered list are the same list' (:248), closing the round-1 gap where TEST-051 demanded a distinct-from-AC-019 boundary statement AC-030's three parts never required. I checked for a residual defect: unlike AC-026/AC-029/AC-003, which split multi-element criteria into one TEST row per element specifically to avoid a 'combined check passes on any one' failure mode (requirements.md:58, :129), AC-030 keeps a single Test ID (TEST-051) for its four parts. This does not rise to a FAIL, however, because the detail block explicitly requires each part to be 'found separately' and lists four independent failing shapes (one per part, acceptance-tests.md:248), which forecloses the OR-semantics risk the split-row precedent exists to prevent; AC-030's own rationale text says 'asserted separately' (requirements.md:95), not '4 TEST rows', so no contradiction with its own stated methodology exists. No other new ambiguity found on re-reading the full document set.

No direct conflict found between requirements, acceptance criteria, constraints, or non-goals. Checked specifically for a collision introduced by the AC-030 fix: requirements.md:93 states the push-failure rule is 'scope-binding... and treating a failed push as an implicit revocation would collide with AC-028's explicit-withdrawal model -- withdrawal is the only way a consent is meant to stop applying mid-session,' which is consistent with AC-028 (requirements.md:75-82) and AC-026's transient-decline model (requirements.md:56-64) rather than contradicting them. AC-019's three-outcome model (requirements.md:207-209) and AC-030 part 4 / AC-026 part 3 both correctly reserve the persistent 'not permitted' outcome for #140's off setting only, with no overlap. Non-goals (requirements.md:263-270) remain consistent with the in-scope REQs (e.g., the pull-direction Non-goal at :267 is reconciled with AC-029 element (e) disclosure requirement without contradiction, since the Non-goal is explicitly 'the gate, not the disclosure').

The Edge Cases section (requirements.md:272-282) enumerates nine material cases -- regeneration between consent and upload (1), destination change (2), later-session/different-operator reuse (3), fabricated consent record (4), ds_profile:none leakage (5), no-DesignSync host (6), .ps1 twin divergence (7), self-defeating negative assertion (8), stale line-number citations (9) -- each mapped to a resolving OQ/REQ/AC/TEST. The push-failure case (AC-030/TEST-051, requirements.md:84-95, acceptance-tests.md:246-248) adds coverage for a failure-mode boundary not previously in the Edge Cases list but is fully traced through REQ-001/AC-030/TEST-051. Negative and boundary coverage also includes decline-is-transient (AC-026/TEST-041-043), withdrawal (AC-028/TEST-046-047), capability-detection failure branches (AC-013/TEST-019-020), and the non-blocking invariant under both absence conditions (AC-015/TEST-022-023). No material negative path implied by the requirements is left untested.

Checked every claim in requirements.md and acceptance-tests.md that touches shared, git-tracked repository state for an explicit re-verification instruction. Found instructions present and specific in each case: protected-file membership (BL-004/BL-005) -- 'Re-verify per the Assumptions section before relying on this' (requirements.md:298-299) plus the general Assumptions bullet at :287; the CI-registration surface (AC-024/TEST-039) -- requirements.md:288 and independently restated at acceptance-tests.md:202 ('Re-derive the three "no" answers above ... rather than trusting this paragraph'); ADR numbering -- requirements.md:289; and blanket file:line staleness -- requirements.md:286 and acceptance-tests.md:259 and investigation.md:317. The human-consent egress gate is the feature's central boundary and is testable. AC-001 (requirements.md:40-48 / TEST-001-003) states all three scope-inheritance branches explicitly. AC-019 (requirements.md:207-209 / TEST-028-030) requires the consent-resolution step to have exactly three named outcomes, with outcome 3 routed to the manual fallback with no upload (TEST-030, acceptance-tests.md:40, :154). AC-026 (decline is transient, requirements.md:56-64) and AC-030 (push failure preserves consent state, requirements.md:84-95) both correctly keep the transient failure/decline cases distinguishable from the persistent 'not permitted' outcome that gates #140's off setting, preventing an implementation from silently manufacturing a standing forbiddance. AC-012 (requirements.md:169) honestly characterizes the Design-Source record as an unenforced audit trace rather than an authorization a gate checks, consistent with docs/THREAT-MODEL.md:12's NOT-Trusted classification of agent self-reports -- this is the correct disclosure for an approval boundary that has no technical enforcement, not a missing boundary.
